package_info.package_name: Modern Solution GmbH & Co. e-commerce connector
package_info.package_versions: unknown (all deployed versions as of June 2021)
package_info.why_malicious: The software stored retail customer passwords in plain text and hardcoded database credentials within the application, exposing sensitive data for all 700,000+ customers. This represents gross negligence in security design, enabling trivial unauthorized access and mass data compromise.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code uses hardcoded credentials to connect to the production customer database, enabling access to all customer data in the database.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Hardcoding database credentials in application code is a critical security flaw, as anyone with access to the code can trivially extract credentials and access sensitive data.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal applications use secure credential storage (e.g., environment variables, secrets management) and restrict database access to only necessary data. Here, credentials are exposed and grant access to all customer data.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: In rare cases, test or demo applications may use hardcoded credentials for non-sensitive data, but never in production or for sensitive customer information.
key_indicators: Credentials grant access to all customer data
No credential rotation or secrets management

execution_context.file_location: customer data storage and retrieval logic
required_permissions: filesystem (if logs or exports are written)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
customer_password = db.query('SELECT password FROM customers WHERE id = ?', customer_id)
# password is stored and returned in plain text
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code retrieves customer passwords from the database, which are stored in plain text, and makes them accessible to any process or user with database access.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Storing passwords in plain text is a severe security vulnerability, as it allows anyone with database access to read all user passwords without restriction.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Best practices require passwords to be hashed and salted, never stored or transmitted in plain text.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: There is no legitimate reason to store production user passwords in plain text.
key_indicators: No evidence of hashing or encryption

attack_chain.action: Application uses hardcoded credentials to connect to the production customer database.
attack_chain.leads_to: Unrestricted access to all customer data, including passwords.

attack_chain.action: Application (or any user with code/database access) queries and retrieves customer passwords stored in plain text.
attack_chain.leads_to: Exposure of all customer credentials; enables mass compromise, credential stuffing, or resale of sensitive data.

behavioral_signatures: Application code containing hardcoded database credentials
Database queries that retrieve or display passwords in plain text
Lack of password hashing or encryption in user data storage
file_indicators: Source code files with connection strings including passwords
Database tables/fields named 'password' with readable values
network_indicators: Unencrypted database connections from application servers
Unusual volume of database queries for password fields
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Scan application source code and configuration files for hardcoded credentials. Audit database schemas and contents for plain text password storage. Monitor for unencrypted database connections and excessive access to sensitive fields. Flag any application or process that retrieves or logs user passwords in plain text.
